---
title: "The two papers"
---

The two published papers answer the course's running-example question in two different ways:

> *In adults with septic shock in the ICU, does a restrictive fluid strategy, compared with usual care, reduce mortality?*

Paper 1 is a randomised trial and Paper 2 is an observational cohort. Reading them side by side shows how the study
design limits what a paper is allowed to claim. Both are **open access**: read them on the publisher's website
with the DOI links below, or download the original PDF here.

## Paper 1: randomised controlled trial

| | |
|:--|:--|
| **Citation** | Boulet N, Quenot J-P, Serrand C, et al. Impact on fluid balance of an optimized restrictive strategy targeting non-resuscitative fluids in intensive care patients with septic shock: a single-blind, multicenter, randomized, controlled, pilot study. *Crit Care.* 2024;28:429. |
| **DOI** | [10.1186/s13054-024-05155-z](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13054-024-05155-z) |
| **PDF** | [Original article (PDF, from the publisher)](files/papers/Paper1_Boulet2024_CritCare_original.pdf) |
| **Design** | Single-blind, multicentre, parallel-group pilot RCT; 48 patients analysed. Primary outcome: cumulative fluid balance at day 5. Registered as NCT04947904. |
| **Reporting guideline** | CONSORT |
| **Licence** | CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 |

## Paper 2: observational cohort

| | |
|:--|:--|
| **Citation** | Hyun D-G, Ahn JH, Huh JW, et al., on behalf of the Korean Sepsis Alliance (KSA) Investigators. Impact of a cumulative positive fluid balance during the first three ICU days in patients with sepsis: a propensity score-matched cohort study. *Ann Intensive Care.* 2023;13:105. |
| **DOI** | [10.1186/s13613-023-01178-x](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13613-023-01178-x) |
| **PDF** | [Original article (PDF, from the publisher)](files/papers/Paper2_Hyun2023_AnnIntensiveCare_original.pdf) |
| **Design** | Propensity score-matched cohort from a prospective multicentre sepsis registry (20 hospitals). Primary outcome: 28-day mortality. |
| **Reporting guideline** | STROBE |
| **Licence** | CC BY 4.0 |

## How the papers are used in the course

| Session | Use |
|:--|:--|
| 2 | Example records for the PubMed search demo; reading Paper 1's abstract against the abstract checklist and looking for spin |
| 3–4 | One question answered by two designs; confounding by indication; which risk-of-bias tool fits each paper |
| 5–6 | Fluid balance as a CRF variable; reading hazard ratios, CIs, p-values and Kaplan–Meier curves; Paper 2 is the published model for the FLUID-ICU analysis |
| 7–8 | Worked examples of titles, abstracts, introductions, results and discussions; reporting guidelines; **Be the reviewer**: the whole class appraises Paper 1 and Paper 2 together with the [critical appraisal checklist](resources.qmd) |

::: {.callout-note}
Both articles are open access. The PDFs offered here are the publishers' original versions, unchanged, shared under
their licences (Paper 1: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; Paper 2: CC BY 4.0). Please cite the papers as given above.
:::
